summary: Use native double addition only when both operands are proven JavaScript Numbers before evaluation.

target.notes: C# double addition matches JavaScript Number addition for already-numeric operands, including NaN, infinities, and signed zero.

caveats: This native rule is valid only while the compiler preserves JavaScript Number as IEEE-754 binary64 and does not introduce integer overflow semantics.
Do not use when either operand may be String, BigInt, Object, Symbol, null, undefined, or Boolean.
